name: Unrefined Ore Sample
summary: In Thousand Needles, an unusual ore draws the Horde's attention. Tatternack Steelforge seeks a sample to judge whether the raw mineral can strengthen the weapons of Warchief Thrall's armies.

sections.title: Mined by the Vermin
sections.body: South of the Barrens, Gravelsnout kobolds dig through the stone beneath the canyon walls of Thousand Needles. Travelers returning north found a curious mineral among slain vermin, unlike the usual veins of Kalimdor. They refused to surrender their prize to the Horde. The kobolds who dig and survey the depths carry raw chunks of the ore from their excavations.

sections.title: Forging for the Warchief
sections.body: At Camp Taurajo, weaponsmith Tatternack Steelforge works under orders from Warchief Thrall to improve the Horde's arms. Travelers who kept knowledge of the deposit angered him; he saw their refusal as an insult to the Horde's war effort. With a raw sample, Tatternack plans to test the mineral's strength and temper, then smelt it and forge a prototype blade for Orgrimmar's approval.

faq.q: Where does this unrefined ore come from?
faq.answer: Gravelsnout kobolds carry the ore from the canyon depths of Thousand Needles, south of the Barrens. Their diggers, surveyors, and leader Gibblesnik live there.

faq.q: Why does Tatternack Steelforge want a sample?
faq.answer: Tatternack works under the Warchief's orders to improve Horde weapons. He wants to inspect and smelt the ore to learn whether it can be forged into stronger arms.

faq.q: Why were the travelers reluctant to part with it?
faq.answer: Horde travelers crossing from Thousand Needles found the ore on a kobold and kept it as a trophy or curiosity. They refused to sell it, even when asked to help the Horde's smithing efforts.

faq.q: Is this ore found anywhere in the Barrens?
aliases: can you mine it in barrens
faq.answer: No. Camp Taurajo lies in the southern Barrens, but the ore must be recovered from kobolds farther south in Thousand Needles.

angles.text: As a blacksmith, you can understand Tatternack's frustration. Testing new ore for strength and durability helps smiths outfit warriors with blades that will not shatter in combat.
As a member of the Horde, you know each new mineral vein in southern Kalimdor could help Thrall's young nation supply its own arms as it secures its borders.
